## Historical ticket scope — superseded where conflicting

Preserved below for release/intent provenance. July wrapper/GF/optional-daemon/build.zig.zon execution instructions are not actionable current authority.

## Outcome

Freeze the v0.2 process-level harness adapter contract and prove it with Codex, Claude, and OpenCode. Control and redacted diagnostics use a versioned JSON-RPC subprocess boundary. There is no C ABI or shared-library SDK.

## Contract

* opaque session and route handles; no token bytes cross the adapter boundary;
* lifecycle: preflight, managed launch, route/lease snapshot, typed transition, repair handoff, teardown;
* exact-model demand and one-alternate outcome vocabulary shared across adapters;
* feature/status discovery is explicit per method; unimplemented methods cannot advertise support;
* local-only redacted events and stable schema versioning;
* adapter-specific auth/provider mechanics stay behind the process boundary.

## Acceptance

1. Checked-in schema and compatibility tests for the new surface version.
2. Codex and Claude managed adapters round-trip lifecycle and redacted status.
3. OpenCode exercises the same contract as the independent conformance adapter.
4. Only the versioned typed scalar extension namespace is tolerated; all other unknown or sensitive fields fail closed, and unsupported capabilities fail explicitly.
5. No C header, shared library, FFI ownership model, or raw credential response is shipped.

Phase-1 PR #475 declares the surface as `planned_unshipped` / `not_implemented`; it does not satisfy adapter round-trip or OpenCode acceptance.

## Outcome

A route in `hard_lineage_invalidated` can return to service only through one managed, provider-owned re-enrollment transaction that proves a newly issued credential lineage and durably resolves both hard authorities. Raw provider login by itself is not clearance.

## Contract

* Acquire the existing per-provider/account flock and the exact upstream-identity flock when available.
* Snapshot only redacted pre-enrollment generation/fingerprint evidence in memory; never persist tokens or provider response bodies.
* Launch the provider-owned login in the account's isolated config/browser boundary.
* Re-read the canonical credential under the same transaction and prove a fresh usable access token plus refresh token and a new credential generation. Same identity is allowed; stale or unchanged rotating-token lineage is not.
* Commit a closed `provider_reenroll_resolved` event and marker transition with crash ordering that never exposes a route between marker removal and durable resolution.
* Update the hard-lineage reducer so only that privately constructed resolution proof can clear the prior hard event. Ordinary `refreshed` rows, manual file edits, stale backups, and raw login success remain unable to clear it.
* On any ambiguity or partial persistence, preserve hard quarantine and emit a redacted typed failure.
* Claude/Codex enrollment remains provider-owned; browser isolation follows TIN-2071. Setup/repair presentation follows TIN-3006.

## Acceptance

* Fake-provider tests cover success, unchanged token lineage, identity drift, canceled login, torn credential, lock contention, crash points on both sides of the durable resolution commit, and restart reduction.
* Tests prove stale backup restoration and ordinary refresh/login rows cannot clear hard state.
* Status/doctor expose whether managed clearance is available and the exact safe next action without implying an unavailable flow.
* Exact-head GF test/check, required CI, and Public Source pass.
* No live provider call or installed/service mutation is required for code acceptance; attended provider proof is a later promotion gate.

## Claim boundary

This is recovery plumbing, not managed continuity proof. TIN-2057 remains unchanged until a separately authorized attended handoff/repair gate passes.

## Outcome

Gate the managed Claude proxy on measured product performance and exact-once correctness, not micro-optimization claims.

## Required budgets

* Local routing/auth overhead before upstream I/O: p95 <= 5 ms, p99 <= 10 ms.
* Sustained SSE throughput: within 5% of direct Claude Code.
* Idle sidecar RSS: <= 20 MiB.
* No starvation at 20 concurrent managed sessions across 50 enrolled accounts.
* Replay memory: 32 MiB/request, 64 MiB/sidecar, 256 MiB/host. Use atomic cross-process reservations with stale-PID cleanup.
* Missing reservation or chunked/unknown-length overflow degrades to stream-once with backpressure; never disk spool.

## Correctness

At most two upstream attempts. Only explicit pre-body 401/403/429 can select one alternate. Provider 5xx passes through. Ambiguous transport, cancellation, partial writes, and started responses never cross accounts. Health/state writes must be atomic and state-change-bounded.

Persistent HTTP clients, buffered header parsing, and parse/write deduplication are implementation tools only when measurement justifies them; do not buffer successful SSE bodies.

## Acceptance

A deterministic fake Anthropic upstream plus a direct-vs-proxy benchmark publishes redacted artifacts for latency percentiles, throughput, RSS, memory-pressure fallback, stale reservation cleanup, attempt counts, and 20x50 lock fairness. This blocks TIN-2057.

TIN-1852.title: [seed] e2e codex/oauth-mux session-lifecycle tests: transaction + resume + concurrent, local + CI, cassette-backed
TIN-1852.description:
## Why (the gap that let TIN-1851 rot for 3 weeks)

The canonical `~/.codex` DB was silently corrupted for \~3 weeks because **no test ever ran a real codex transaction, a resume, or concurrent sessions**. Unit-green against fakes (incl. the cassette adapters, PRs #354/#357) cannot catch a corrupted *shared* DB. "login status / preflight green / N/N tests pass" were repeatedly substituted for a real end-to-end check. **unit-green ≠ working.**

The codex session lifecycle is a clear, replayable state — model it properly.

## Cases to cover (seed; not fully scoped yet)

* single **transaction**: `codex exec "…"` returns a model reply; records a healthy `~/.codex` rollout path; 0 new `oauth-mux-codex-` rows.
* single **resume**: `codex exec resume <id>` loads the prior transcript (token count reflects history) with 0 `state db returned stale rollout path`.
* **concurrent** sessions/resumes: ≥2 simultaneous, both succeed, 0 `SessionAuthorityLocked`, 0 new poisoned rows.
* both **stock** (native \~/.codex) AND **muxxed** (`TINYLAND_CODEX_MUX_SESSIONS=1`) — the muxxed lane gated on TIN-1851.
* a **DB-integrity invariant**: after any run, `0` rows in `threads.rollout_path` point outside `~/.codex` (regression guard for the temp-home poisoning).

## Vehicle

The cassette recorder/replayer (PR #357 / TIN-1823) is the deterministic-replay path for the muxxed/API side; live smoke for the stock path. Wire into the test suite + CI so a regression of TIN-1851 fails a check instead of corrupting a real DB.

## Status

**Seed only** — captured so it isn't lost; not in-scope for the current damage-control sprint. Demonstrated manually on neo 2026-06-02 (single tx + resume + 2 concurrent native, all green); this issue is to make that automated + CI-enforced.

project_core.name: Omux · native lifecycle + core
project_core.summary: Resident daemon, typed lifecycle, encrypted custody, compatible generic resources and preservation of historical evidence.
project_core.description:
Experimental, unshipped native reset. Install Omux, authorize sources once, and use ordinary application commands. Supported handoff preserves the same process and native session/history/tools/approvals with no routine prompt. No wrapper, alternate home, restart, shipped Codex fork, browser automation or synthetic promotion proves this outcome.

Authority: [active reset](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/plans/omux-native-account-lifecycle-reset-2026-10-02.md>), [charter](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/product/charter.md>), [acceptance](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/product/user-stories.md>), [support gates](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/product/support-and-completeness.md>), [evidence](<https://github.com/Jesssullivan/oauth-mux/blob/codex/omux-native-reset/docs/implementation/native-reset-evidence-2026-10-02.md>). Builds/tests/generators/packages/checks run locally through locked Nix + Bazel/Bazelisk. No automatic CI or GF requirement. Historical v0.1.15 and reviewed evidence retain their original claims; tracker completion cannot promote live support.

## Current workstream

Own identity/account/source/grant/resource/observation/binding/lease separation, verified automatic enrollment, detachment versus disconnect, pause/drain/forget/tombstones and explicit re-enrollment. Complete renewal/adoption/revoke APIs, bounded std.Io.Threaded/libcurl multi/SQLite ownership and XDG conformance. Keep native stores and reviewed historical documents/evidence.

## Historical project charter — superseded 2026-10-02

The following text is preserved for provenance, not current execution or capability authority.

## Charter

Own the v0.2 authority reset, pure broker data model, HarnessAdapter seam, main.zig vertical extraction, and replace-delete train.

## Deliverables

* Canonical plan, authority map, and deletion ledger.
* Public CLI reset: setup, claude, codex, accounts, status, doctor, service, repair, version.
* Pure ModelDemand, RouteObservation, EvidenceProvenance, AccountLease, BrokerDecision, and ProxyAttempt types.
* Versioned JSON-RPC surface; no C ABI.
* Removal of the experimental socket daemon, restart/supervisor product paths, proof-only public verbs, retired npm residue, unproven provider built-ins, and superseded docs after replacement proof.

Builds/tests/generators/packages/checks run locally through locked Nix + Bazel/Bazelisk. No automatic CI or GF requirement. Historical v0.1.15 and reviewed evidence retain their original claims; tracker completion cannot promote live support.

## Current workstream

Own NAC-001–018, private control/adapter APIs, per-request IDs, binding isolation, narrow materialization, pre-acceptance budget, safe native detach and account-bound transport/context invalidation. Candidate is rust-v0.157.0 / 00c972ed5d6ff6499317fd41b7f23605b8e6850d, native_support=false. Omux ships no Codex fork; upstream availability and live conformance remain blocking. OpenCode deferred.

## Charter

* Codex remains the reference managed harness and must retain existing live proof.
* Claude implements the same route/credential/session decision contract through its request sidecar.

* No Gemini subscription OAuth piggybacking and no broad provider catalog.

C ABI work is canceled until a real embedder exists.

Experimental, unshipped native reset. Install Omux, authorize sources once, and use ordinary application commands. No wrapper, alternate home, restart, shipped Codex fork, browser automation or synthetic promotion proves this outcome.

Builds/tests/generators/packages/checks run locally through locked Nix + Bazel/Bazelisk. No automatic CI or GF requirement. Historical v0.1.15 and reviewed evidence retain their original claims; tracker completion cannot promote live support.

## Current workstream

Own SC-01–11 and NAC-018 evidence; separate source, fixture, installation, native and live classes. Show independent grant/readiness/entitlement/lifecycle and freshness. Current experimental service has no contractual SLA or invented human on-call. Reliability objectives require defined measurement windows/evidence before promotion.

## Historical project charter — superseded 2026-10-02

The following text is preserved for provenance, not current execution or capability authority.

## Charter

* Local-only trace IDs, bounded redacted event rings, statusline, doctor, and report.
* Transition notifications for successful switches and durable action-required states.
* Daily no-spend schema checks and weekly budgeted micro-spend adapter compatibility.
* Property, fake-upstream, cassette, process-chaos, performance, and release proof.
* 2xClaude + 2xCodex golden evidence.
* Three clean non-maintainer beta installs, including one Linux user.
* Menu-bar snapshot contract designed now; companion ships after broker GA.

No prompts, responses, tokens, cookies, raw identities, or provider page dumps enter evidence.

carrier_issue.description:
## Outcome

Sting is the intended daily remote development seat. Complete and preserve the real edit → signed commit → push → PR → review workflow alongside working SSH, tmux/cmux and eGreg. Neo can keep running concurrent work; it is not frozen for a ceremony.

## Adoption evidence

The 2026-08-31 receipt in comment `f357b473-6456-4afd-bf92-089a7a22bf28` records all three measured criteria: LAN interactive login, continuously alive `main`, and Sting-produced signed PR [tinyland-inc/lab#1595](https://linear.app/tinyland/review/docssting-support-live-migration-and-retire-ceremony-gates-c34185263808). Review and merge remained outstanding at that receipt.

The 2026-09-12 takeover confirms existing `main` and `egreg-lab` sessions at `/tmp/tmux-1000/default`. The current CLI default socket differs; attach the existing server rather than interpreting the other socket's absence as session loss. Current unqualified `who` is empty, so no new interactive-login receipt is asserted.

## Remaining closure

Lab [tinyland-inc/lab#1595](https://linear.app/tinyland/review/docssting-support-live-migration-and-retire-ceremony-gates-c34185263808) merged through normal protections at 2026-09-13T00:44:10Z, merge commit `1d8079fb0b88082fbd0f846404a5166e19bf1c57`: [tinyland-inc/lab#1595](https://linear.app/tinyland/review/docssting-support-live-migration-and-retire-ceremony-gates-c34185263808). The September repair removes superseded stillness, exclusion and stop-writer prose and its literal test assertions. Runtime continuity and full-state coverage remain distinct from this completed documentation merge.

The September carry has placed eleven additional home trees on `/srv/fast-local` with home symlinks. Recovered Codex history is preserved in a standalone SQLite snapshot under `state/provider-snapshots/neo/20260909T093450Z`. The separately reviewed state_5 insert-only/path-update adapter has now completed live integration; recovered thread-history composition remains offline. The operator authorized treating `ems-jess-dev-wt` as archival payload: its broken `.git` pointer was removed on both hosts, with payload preserved. Live state_5 integration is complete; the recovered thread-history candidate remains preserved offline.

C2 auto-fire is disarmed by `d721a04a` and its amendments; the expired August deadline never triggers a reframe or session shutdown. The obsolete C2 execution blocks and queue sequence have been removed from this description. Prior observations and ratifications remain in comments. [TIN-3080](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-3080/relocate-egreg-emacs-daemon-honeysting-new-e)'s eGreg disposition follows its own completion record; historical storage incidents do not impose an unratified avoidance of `/srv/fast-local`.

## Configuration reconciliation receipt

Eight copied configuration links targeted a Neo-only Nix store generation absent on Sting. No corresponding files existed in Sting's active Home Manager generation. Repaired cmux, ghostty, linear-gsuite, the explicitly Neo-named storage registry, and four tinyland/vscode links to their preserved resolved incoming files under `/srv/fast-local/jess/state/config-carry/neo-20260912/resolved`; original link definitions remain in `source-links`. No readable native managed setting was overwritten. The fish 4.3 migration file had an empty `fish_key_bindings`; restored `fish_default_key_bindings`, preserved the original in that same carry namespace, and verified a new interactive fish shell without the warning. Existing shells were not restarted.

The operator is beginning active work on Sting in spear_resumes and eGreg. Those workspaces remain dual-writer protected. `/home/jess` remains the login home; git/Claude/Codex/gstack resolve onto `/srv/fast-local`. `.config` and `.pi` remain on `/home`. Lab [tinyland-inc/lab#1595](https://linear.app/tinyland/review/docssting-support-live-migration-and-retire-ceremony-gates-c34185263808) is now merged through the normal protected process.

## eGreg parity gap — manual comparison

Operator manually fetched spear_resumes before the parity check; matching HEAD there does not prove migration delivery. eGreg was not at parity: Sting main4775fa6 was5 commits behind Neo mainff040f6 and42 behind active3617081, which Sting lacked. Neo lane-docs has1 changed path and lane-graph13, plus main .serena/project.yml. Eight registered Sting worktrees lack index files; three retain README payload and five do not. HEAD-resolution alone was insufficient prior acceptance.

Preserved all Neo eGreg refs in `/srv/fast-local/jess/state/git-carry/neo/eGreg/20260913/neo-egreg.bundle`, SHA256 `24eb80be2550e1f77729fbeabb698bf987e674aa015a2768d5c171de3805ff68`, and imported into separate `refs/carry/neo/20260913/*`. Native Sting HEAD remained4775fa6. This is object/ref custody, not active-checkout parity. All four current Neo eGreg checkouts have additionally been captured using the native Rust Git adapter and imported into neutral carry refs. Real Neo→Sting native transfer verified both bundle hashes: cold transferred 1,788,751 bytes from 1,886,317 source bytes; repeat reused both files with zero source reads or transfer. Current Neo checkout restoration is complete: `eGreg.worktrees/neo-active-20260913` plus `lane-console`, `lane-docs`, and `lane-graph`, all at 36170812ba41427e71614981b86f16d330229b4a. The native d4699b8 mover preserved their branch names and dirty state. Independently compared index-entry hashes and normalized staged/unstaged binary diffs against Neo: all match. All four reverse gitdir pointers verified and roots0700. Existing Sting main remains4775fa6. The eight historical worktrees now have reconstructed committed baselines under the operator's explicit approval. Original payload and administration are preserved under `state/git-carry/sting/eGreg/historical-baselines-20260913`; all eight baseline checks passed, active main and worktree registrations remained unchanged. Unknown original staging was not recovered or claimed recovered.

Remaining portable local-share payload: pnpm was absent on Sting. Preserved 101,585 regular files and 12 links (1,262,474,605 bytes including links) under `state/local-share-carry/neo-20260912/pnpm`, private root0700. This is preserved cache/tool payload, not activation of Darwin executables or Neo Nix-store launchers. TCFS registries list three noncolliding devices, but only Sting's input currently verifies cryptographically. Native self-import validates Sting's configured key and active registry; Neo's incoming registry fails signature verification. Neo's live file and carried copy have identical SHA256 `5390616319deeac2ee7cd47bd9c3c4a6dec121bad943baf94d6afe763e971c4e`, so the defect predates this carry. Signed and GitHub-verified commit `dbf9d26a959c2c12b0cefdcff07491ca25164827` provides a tested candidate-only native import command. Real candidate generation correctly refused; no signature bypass, rekeying, active registry replacement, or identity change occurred. A publication window alone does not resolve an invalid source signature.

`spear_resumes`: both main checkouts clean at148b9b52 after the operator's manual update. Recovered missing Neo branch `jess/tin-3750-hermetic-artifacts` atd052e410 on Sting via create-only ref update; bundle SHA256 `7e21394995e79ca529102dc57bf8029d2f599422b04fc9fa232647f575d8e036` retained in `state/git-carry/neo/spear_resumes/20260913/neo-heads.bundle`. Sting-only dirty `registry-default-20260813` captured by native d4699b8 with filesystem metadata; bundle SHA256 `83b81320764d95964215419cbec621bc71f12f3291fd8544537429d33f212989` retained in `state/git-carry/sting/spear_resumes/20260913/registry-default-capture/capture.bundle` and imported into Neo neutral `refs/carry/sting/20260913/registry-default/*`. Both working checkouts untouched. This repairs observed custody gaps without claiming estate-wide parity.

## Native transfer and provider validation

Native mover commit d4699b8 delivered and restored the four current eGreg worktrees. Four fresh bundles crossed Neo→Sting in8.91s (3,772,926 transferred bytes), warmrepeat0.28s with zero source reads/transfer; all hashes match. Larger sealed23-file corpus Sting→Neo acceptance transferred1,337,244,921bytes in135.69s from an already warmed source store, with zero original-source bytes reread. Repeat0.14s reused23files with zero wire/source bytes; all23SHA256 values match retained source hashes. A registered interruption test resumed after one committed file and completed remainingtwo without source rereads. These are measured directions/corpora, not an rclone comparison or a no-directory-rewalk claim.

Native hydration completed 6,708 files (415,480,447,268 output bytes), with compressed inputs retained and identities validated. The approved live state_5 adapter completed: 1,739 rows inserted, 10,248 paths corrected, zero runtime conflicts. Post-apply validation records 11,235 threads, unchanged schema and 52 migration records, zero foreign-key violations, and quick_check OK. All 114 historical missing-file records retain their original path pairs. Final Neo cutoff: 2026-09-13T01:03:30.434801059Z; later activity is not covered by this cutoff. Source snapshots and pre-apply backup hashes remain verified. Receipts: `/srv/fast-local/jess/state/provider-snapshots/sting/20260913-final-cutoff/`. No database file was replaced and no session stopped. Recovered-history composition remains offline: 266,352 records imported into the candidate, 506,729 existing items preserved, and 438 conflicting/orphan/control cases retained separately.

## Current operator decisions and estate scope

Operator explicitly chose to keep the invalid full Neo registry archived. Sting's active registry is unchanged; a separately recovered older `neo.local` subset verifies under the original signature, and its signed union candidate is retained but not activated. No rekeying or signature bypass is authorized. The later `macbook-neo` entry remains preserved but unverified.

Operator authorized preserving all existing files in the eight older eGreg worktrees and reconstructing their committed baselines. Existing files and administration must be retained before reconstruction; unknown original staging must not be represented as recovered. The four newly restored current Neo worktrees and active Sting main are outside that repair set.

Operator reiterated that eGreg is one of many repositories and full estate migration is required. Per-repository mover acceptance is not estate-wide coverage. Read-only repository/worktree comparison and bounded native batch execution are now in progress. Import-only custody must remain distinct from a usable restored workspace; active destination work must not be overwritten.

## Native estate acceptance — 2026-09-13

Completed and checked on Sting: 13 missing-index repairs, 24 ordinary absent worktrees restored, 1 retained-registration payload recovery ([TIN-1449](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-1449/e5-observability-slos-per-tenant-dashboards-ttfch-probe-poison)), and 6 payload-only workspaces reattached. Captured HEADs, semantic indexes and reverse Git pointers were checked; active destination work remains untouched. These match recorded source snapshots, not later Neo commits. The two retained bulkload/DarwinNicUtil indexes recover dated staging, not unknown later staging. Other registered-payload recoveries remain in flight; a resolving HEAD alone is not payload completion.

Signed 562d277 includes configuration-aware standalone restoration, guarded retained-registration recovery and persistence timing instrumentation. 52 scoped tests, formatting, clippy and Linux/Darwin releases passed. Later source changes (streaming Git-object restoration, bounded persistence parallelism and directory durability) await integrated validation. Metadata censuses remain; no never-rewalk claim.

Measured comparison: isolated APFS-cloned 23-file corpus, 242,605,606 source bytes; local copy on Neo, nice19, one repetition per run, OS caches not flushed. Full BLAKE3 and mode/link checks ran outside timing. Instrumented run2: native initial 53,848.545 ms, 226,762,914 transferred content bytes; native resume 4.840 ms, zero source/content bytes. Actual rclone initial 1,082.360 ms, resume 141.069 ms; its byte counters are unmeasured. Native initial is about 49.75 times slower and resume about 29.15 times faster: not an overall performance win or a network benchmark. Chunk persistence measured 5,876 calls and 104.702 seconds summed worker time, including 35.135 seconds file sync and 31.734 seconds directory sync (5,743 each). Worker sums are not additive wall-time shares or isolated causal proof. Receipt: /Users/[host-local user redacted]/git/tummycrypt/.bulkload-bench-real-ee15653/run2-instrumented.log. Run1 remains retained beside it.

Not full-estate completion. Blahaj and some lab/GF restorations remain held on differing common info/exclude policies; no global policy edit occurred. Fresh configuration-aware Legalab and Medical captures completed and were delivered for restoration. Both source-change refusals from the 32-item pass succeeded on one bounded retry. The unchanged 103-item same-HEAD index capture plan is now running; its first seven captures were delivered. Chapel refused with GIT_INVENTORY_MALFORMED and is being investigated separately, not excluded. Original source captures continue without signals.

Recovered history remains offline pending explicit historical-restoration disposition: 3,511 turns and 262,043 items are absent from live history, all associated with currently live state5 thread IDs. No deletion tombstones exist, so first-import history cannot distinguish never-migrated rows from intentionally deleted rows. No history activation, projection-offset changes, database replacement or session stop occurred.

Ruling: R-HOOK-CONVERGENCE-20261004, R-C11 (validated on sting, then admin-merged), R-N13.

- **mcp_project_audit**: the test now checks that the global agent-project hook is advisory. The strict `--fail-on-*` check stays on agent-project.nix.

- **host_local_become**: the preflight now runs with a `python3` that points at the test's own interpreter, which has PyYAML. I added a test that the fallback host list still covers every Linux host.

**2026-10-04 06:30 EDT — R-C293 adversarial verify (lab#2202). Tests pass on sting. Not merged.**

Rulings: R-C293, R-C292, R-C11, OI-1002-Q16.

**What changed in #2202.** It is rebased onto #2196's pushed R-C292 head `cafac1552` and is now at signed head `147facb2f`.
- R-C293 allows a bare 64-hex value under `digest` and `image_digest`. So those two cases moved out of the R-C292 blocked-cases test.
- **Fake digest keys** such as `api_key_digest`. Decision: a key ending in `_digest` or `_sha256` is trusted only when nothing on the line looks like a secret name. The word list now also catches:
  - any word ending in `key` or `keys` (`master_key_sha256`, `masterKey_digest`)
  - `pass`, which covers passphrase and passcode
  - auth, bearer, session, cookie, salt, pepper, mnemonic, and `otp` as a standalone word
  - matching ignores case

  This also blocks public-key fingerprints such as `host_key_sha256:`. Blocking is the safe direction. Tests were added for each case.
- **Path spoofing** (a file named `provisioner/tenants/...` in another repo): no path is trusted. R-C293 adds no path rule. The existing skip for source-file extensions (.json, .yaml, .py) depends only on the extension, not the path. A new test puts a value under a non-digest key in scanned files at three spoofed paths, and each one blocks.
- **Residuals we accept**, which a check that reads one line of the diff at a time cannot close:
  - a secret-named parent key on a different line (`api_key:` and then `  digest: <hex>`)
  - deliberately misspelled names such as `s3cret_digest`

## 2026-10-04 ~07:30Z: lab seat (neo), R-C286 (operator interview): attended repair of PZM's Nix DB

**R-C286:** repair PZM's corrupt `/nix/var/nix/db/db.sqlite` now, following the 2026-09-26 precedent. Steps:
1. Before anything else, state who is logged in on PZM, any tmux servers and any agent processes there (R-N11 service-lifecycle precondition).
2. Stop the named job `system/systems.determinate.nix-daemon` with `launchctl bootout`. This is permitted named-service lifecycle; it is not an agent, tmux or session surface.
3. Back up `db.sqlite` plus its `-wal` and `-shm` files next to the original with a dated suffix.
4. Rebuild the database: `sqlite3 .recover` (or dump and restore) into a new DB, then REINDEX. Run integrity_check; it must report ok.
5. Swap the new DB in.
6. Start the daemon again with `launchctl bootstrap` / `kickstart`.
7. Run `nix-store --verify` (without `--repair` unless needed), then the serialized GC to free `/nix`.

No reboot, no mount changes and no GF services. If integrity_check is not ok or the daemon fails to start, stop and report; the backup stays in place.

- **How R-C246 tells cmux apart:** a `Match originalhost sting exec` block comes first in the cmux ssh drop-in, `00-tinyland-cmux-connection.conf`. It checks the name of ssh's **parent process** and matches only when it is exactly `cmux`. On a match it resets ControlMaster/ControlPath/ControlPersist to the OpenSSH defaults, so cmux falls back to its own `/tmp/cmux-ssh-<uid>-%C` socket. Any other caller, including agent ssh from bash, keeps the shared `~/.ssh/cm-%C` master. The parent name is used because cmux 0.64.25 picks its socket once, from its own `ssh -G`, and that child has no environment variable only cmux sets. You can turn it off with `tinyland.ssh.cmuxConnection.plainHostCmuxRouting` (default true).

**2026-10-02 NET1 receipt (R-C141, lab seat on neo)**: read-only profile of why `cmux ssh sting` from neo is slow and flaky. Nothing was changed, restarted or signalled (R-N11).

Note: `docs/agent-notes/2026-10-02-TIN-3692-neo-sting-ssh-profile.md`, landed in PR #2083 (admin-merged 2026-10-02T13:04:10Z, merge commit 45634903e). The worktree has been removed.

Key numbers:
- Path to sting is direct LAN through Tailscale, with no DERP and no MTU problem.
- 50 pings to sting showed 168 ms average and 402 ms max with 0 % loss. Pings to the **LAN gateway** were the same (173/430 ms), as a burst-release sawtooth. RSSI is -45 dBm. awdl0 and Universal Control are active.
- ssh connect times:
  - warm mux: p50 0.49 s, p95 1.20 s
  - cold Tailscale SSH: p50 0.57 s, p95 1.15 s
  - cold native OpenSSH: p50 1.42 s, p95 2.09 s
- Echo RTT in an open session: p50 about 320 ms over both Tailscale SSH and native sshd. 50 MB transfers ran at 3.5-5 MB/s.
- Sting: load 35 on 32 CPUs, 6 GiB RAM available, `/srv/fast-local` at 47 %, no OOM kills. The audit log shows a Tailscale SSH login from neo every ~5 s, from the cmux port-scan probe.
- Neo: load 26 and swap 5.4 of 6 GiB, with another lane running a local `go test` on neo.

Causes, most likely first:
1. Neo's Wi-Fi stalls about 400 ms per cycle (likely AWDL).
2. Neo is starved for memory and CPU.
3. All cmux traffic shares one mux master, including the port-scan probe every 2-3 s and a 120 GB bulk upload earlier.
4. Each probe opens a new Tailscale SSH session on sting, which adds churn there.
5. Login-shell init costs about 0.3 s per new session.
6. Tailscale SSH vs native sshd makes no measurable difference.

Fix options A-G are in the note and need rulings. They include wired Ethernet on neo, AWDL/Universal Control changes, a separate ControlPath for cmux, a lower cmux probe rate, faster shell init, and a Go build guard on neo.

**Run:** after the lead's `nix store gc --max 4G` on PZM (/nix 11 GiB free, 80 percent at the start), a clean worktree on neo at lab main 3d755193b (carries 828cc769d), SSH_AUTH_SOCK on the gpg-agent socket, no override flag. It failed earlier than before, at the new phase 1:

```
The Neo producer on petting-zoo-mini exited 69; producer diagnostic: stage=realize-substitute command_exit_code=1.
macbook-neo : ok=101 changed=0 unreachable=0 failed=1 skipped=118
```

The playbook took 17 m 39 s. neo stays on generation 61 (2026-09-24 13:26) with the pre-fix hook.

**Retained diagnostic** (realize-3d755193b...-substitute-b335a807....stderr, 219,545 bytes, read on PZM; nothing token-shaped in the lines quoted):
- Phase 1 did its job: 226 paths copied from the caches, with evaluation warnings only.
- Every error is one of two kinds, and nothing else appears:
  - 248 blocks read `error: Cannot build '/nix/store/...drv'.` / `Reason: local builds are disabled (max-jobs = 0)` / `Hint: set 'max-jobs' to a non-zero value to enable local builds, or configure remote builders via 'builders'`. These are the local-only derivations, for example agent-process-safety-audit, bashrc and the hm_ files.
  - 295 blocks read `Reason: N dependencies failed.`, ending at home-manager-generation.
- The one error the producer accepts, `error: Unable to start any build; either increase '--max-jobs' or enable remote builds.` (NO_LOCAL_BUILDS, line 58), appears 0 times.

**Cause:** `substitution_outcome()` in scripts/validation/neo-hm-remote-producer.py accepts exactly one error block that equals NO_LOCAL_BUILDS. Nix 2.35.2 under Determinate 3.22.5 reports the same condition per derivation in the new wording, so an otherwise clean substitution phase is refused. This is a parser mismatch, not a PZM fault.

**Proposed fix (a lab PR):** make `substitution_outcome()` also accept the 2.35 shape as "builds-remain". Every error block must be either a `Cannot build` block whose Reason is exactly `local builds are disabled (max-jobs = 0)` with that exact Hint, or a `Cannot build` block whose Reason is `N dependencies failed.`, with at least one of the first kind, return code 1 and nothing else. Any substitution, network, signature, disk, auth or evaluation line still refuses. Add a test built from this file's shape. Then rerun the switch unchanged.

**After the run:** PZM /nix is 6.6 GiB free (89 percent), because phase 1 fetched about 4.4 GiB. That is below main's 8 GiB disk floor, so the next rerun needs space again; a gc that keeps the just-fetched paths rooted would not free them. The neo worktree is removed and nothing else changed.

## Drift-tolerant capture — design record (R25 compliance; design lane 2026-09-22, implementation pending)

Read against merged main `8976397`. Nothing is coded yet; this is the record so the implementation PR can be checked against it.

**Why capture refuses today.** `reusable_capture_key` (git_carry.rs ~247–321) hashes 11 unconditional inputs: canonical worktree + common-dir paths, the **full `for-each-ref` inventory** (defect a: every sibling worktree writes into this namespace), HEAD, symbolic HEAD, the full index bytes, `info/exclude`, the stash reflog, the **entire filesystem census** with stat identity per seat (defect b: cargo rewriting one ignored file moves the key), config bytes, and the shallow frontier. The post-pass guard (~599–607) compares all of these as one whole and refuses `GIT_AUTHORITY_CHANGED` on any difference; `raw_tree.rs` :37–52 also refuses when a seat's stat identity changes between census and byte read.

**Design (follows the PR #595 sidecar precedent exactly, so no retained bundle or journal is invalidated):**
- A new typed `CaptureDrift { rows: [DriftRow{kind ∈ RefAdded/RefChanged/RefRemoved/SeatAdded/SeatChanged/SeatRemoved, name}] }`, sorted, capped at 65,536 rows (`BudgetExceeded` beyond — unbounded drift is indistinguishable from a rebuild).
- The monolithic post-pass guard is split: **refs diff → drift**; **census rows diff (stat identity) → drift**; nested-worktree census, config, shallow frontier, **index, HEAD → still hard refusals**. In-pass read drift in `raw_tree.rs` becomes `SeatChanged` (pre-check moves before the fast-import `M` line; a post-read mismatch finishes the committed `data N` obligation deterministically and emits `D <path>` so the seat leaves the tree). One byte pass, no rewalk.
- Drifted seats are **omitted** from both the worktree tree and `filesystem-v1`; the drift sidecar is the statement that they are absent.
- Carried as `refs/carry-export/capture-drift-v1` (in-bundle, only when non-empty; no restore path reads it) and `{name}.drift` beside `{name}.base` in the corpus. `Capture` postcard gains no field. **Drift is not hashed into the key** (it describes a pass, not a repo state).
- New outcome **`captured-with-drift`** (an `Ok`, so exit 0 falls out; `reason=drift=NNN` in the existing tuple, layout-safe). `estate.rs` second-key check compares key *parts* field-by-field so only inventory/rows differences become drift.
- R25 incremental pass: on key mismatch, diff previous vs current key parts; if confined to inventory + seats with changed stat identity, capture only those into a delta bundle over the existing prerequisite machinery (`capture-extended-from-drift`); seats with unchanged identity are never opened again (bytes_read counter proves it).
- Separability, stated plainly: refs and worktree files are separable from HEAD and index in the current code. A lane in a **sibling** worktree will now succeed (yesterday's refusal #2). A lane that **commits inside the captured worktree** still refuses (HEAD + index move). That is the honest limit of this change.
- 15 named tests, including the operator-requested one (`concurrent_ref_creation_and_file_mutation_during_one_capture_succeed_with_drift`), a clean-capture byte-identity test, a pre-change-key reuse test, and the never-rewalk proof (`a_second_pass_after_drift_rereads_only_the_drifted_seats`).

**Open questions for the operator** (answered in the next interview; defaults the implementation will use until ruled otherwise are in parentheses): (1) R25 reading — re-reading a seat that demonstrably changed is permitted; only unchanged-identity seats are never re-read (yes). (2) drifted seat omitted vs captured at post-drift bytes (omitted). (3) apply refuses or silently proceeds when the destination already holds a seat the drift list says was never captured (proceeds; recorded in receipt). (4) `shared::export_base` stays a hard refusal (yes). (5) concurrent `git gc` pruning a captured-then-deleted ref before bundle write: loud failure acceptable (yes). (6) HEAD/index tolerance: file a follow-up issue now (yes). (7) drift rows in the receipt vs count only (count only, layout-safe).

Sequencing: lands **after** #597 (rebuildable omission), which is being rebased onto main now; both touch the census walk.

## Window 2 cannot be probed — and the pre-ratified C2 may be answering the wrong question

Recorded 2026-08-21 during the R40 estate reground, six days before the deadline. **No sting contact was made in producing this.** Everything below is from this issue, the continuity-incident doc, and the repository.

### The three criteria all require touching the held host

| # | Criterion | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interactive logins visible in `who` | a session on sting |
| 2 | A continuously-alive named tmux session | a session on sting |
| 3 | One full edit → commit → PR → review **sting-side** | working on sting |

The `STING_CONTINUITY_INCIDENT_2026-08-17` hold forbids SSH, console, host, cluster, storage, runner, Home Manager, TCFS and Bulkload operations until the Exit gate is satisfied **and the specific role and action have their own attended readmission decision**. Readmission of one role does not lift another's.

So the watch condition —

> Re-run the three probes at or before 2026-08-27T12:12Z and record the result as a comment on this issue. Absence of a probe record at the deadline is itself a lapse and triggers C2.

— is unsatisfiable while the hold stands. Not "hard": unsatisfiable. Both branches of the watch condition converge on C2, so **the outcome is already determined** and, per this issue's own text, no interview is owed.

### The part that is worth a decision anyway

C2 was ratified on 2026-08-12 against a specific observed cause: window 1 lapsed with *zero adoption signal* — `who` empty, no tmux server ever started, `last` showing only reboots. Nobody used the seat. Re-labelling it an agent host is a sound inference **from that cause**.

Window 2 will lapse from a different cause. The continuity incident opened 2026-08-17, five days into the window, and the hold has stood since. A seat nobody may log into cannot produce login records, so window 2 measures the hold, not adoption.

Executing C2 on that basis would record "sting is not a daily human dev seat" as a finding, when the evidence for window 2 supports only "sting was unavailable". Those are different claims, and only the first is what C2 was ratified to conclude.

Three ways forward, none of which touch the host:

1. **Let C2 execute as written.** Consistent with the standing ratification, and window 1's evidence independently supports the conclusion. Cost: the durable record attributes the re-label partly to a window that measured nothing.
2. **Execute C2 but amend the rationale** to cite window 1's zero-signal probe as the sole evidence, and record window 2 as void-by-hold. Same end state, honest provenance.
3. **Extend to window 3, clocked from Exit-gate satisfaction** rather than from a calendar date, so the next window measures adoption rather than availability.

Recommendation: **2**. The conclusion is already carried by window 1's evidence, so no new probe is needed to justify it — but the record should not claim window 2 as corroboration when it is silence caused by a hold.

### Repo-side work is proceeding

An analysis pass is partitioning #1098, #1291, #1019 and #1330 into strictly repo-side versus host-touching halves, so whatever can land without host contact does. Every partition is being independently checked by a skeptic for changes that *look* inert but are not. Nothing from that lane will be landed without passing that check.

Note also that this issue is currently `In Review`, which is accurate — flagging only because a separate finding in this reground identified 183 merge-correlated state transitions from the PR-merge automation across four repos, so state on any issue with attached PRs is worth reading with suspicion right now.

## eGreg pin advance (R26 Q4) — BLOCKED at step 2, no PR opened

Ran the operator-ratified ceremony ("advance the eGreg preview pin 765a6d8d → a58bc9a8 via the private-input cache publisher") against main `f5ea9203`. **Stopped at step 2 without improvising.** No PR was opened, no asset was minted, no release was mutated, no files were changed.

### The recorded procedure is not executable as written

`config/egreg-preview-pin.json` → `adjudication.advance_procedure` (written 2026-08-16) prescribes:

> (2) `just nix-private-input-publish <PR> <HEAD>` … to append the mirror asset

The publisher is **hardcoded single-input to GloriousFlywheel** and cannot mint an eGreg asset. In `tools/nixprivateinput/contract.go`:

```go
sourceRepository = "tinyland-inc/GloriousFlywheel"  // :33
inputName        = "gloriousflywheel"               // :34
```

- `publisher.go:164 validateCandidateLock` reads only `nodes[inputName]`, and at `:211` rejects any lock diff touching another node.
- `:214` requires locked `owner==tinyland-inc` / `repo==GloriousFlywheel`; `:230` requires the *gloriousflywheel* rev to have advanced.
- `:524` hardcodes `archive_name = "tinyland-inc-GloriousFlywheel-"+rev+".tar.gz"`; `:528` emits the constant `source_repository`, which the workflow then checks out — so even the source fetch targets GF.
- There is not one `egreg` string anywhere in `tools/nixprivateinput/`.

Confirmed empirically, not just by reading: feeding `validateCandidateLock` the exact egreg-only lock advance the ceremony prescribes returns

```
candidate flake.lock may change only nodes.gloriousflywheel
```

### The asymmetry worth remembering

The **consumer** side is fully generic — `validateContract` iterates `registry.inputs[]`, derives `<owner>-<repo>-<rev>.tar.gz` (`:446`) and enforces rev+narHash parity (`:478`), validating all three inputs happily. Only **minting** is GF-only. eGreg assets validate fine; they just can't be published by the publisher.

**How 765a6d8d got there:** `0add09ae` (2026-08-12) states the asset was uploaded **manually**. The publisher landed the *next day* in `ef7e2f14` (2026-08-13), declaring itself "the sole append-only publisher" — but it was only ever built for GF. The eGreg lane was never migrated onto it, and the 08-16 procedure assumed a generalization that does not exist.

### All three recorded target facts re-verified CORRECT

- rev `a58bc9a8f0ca541711d019414119f17ee55cd9e1` = eGreg `main` HEAD, signed, GitHub-verified, "fix(writing): direct-async must not inherit the remote login shell (#101)"
- narHash `sha256-D3mc6QAlEZ1sb6Np2eZ/g7vzfYuYLR/XwnN6dtRBGTQ=` — confirmed by live `nix flake prefetch`
- lastModified `1786563055` — matches committer date 2026-08-12T19:30:55Z

Release `nix-private-input-cache-v1` holds 4 assets; **no** `Jesssullivan-egreg-a58bc9a8….tar.gz` exists. Contract `audit` at main is GREEN (`ok:true, input_count:3`), so nothing is currently broken — the pin simply stays at 765a6d8d.

### Decision needed (2 options)

1. **Generalize the publisher** — parameterize the input (dispatch input name; derive `sourceRepository`/`archive_name` from the candidate lock node). Correct and durable; needs its own PR + ratification since it edits a protected release-mutating workflow and its Go tool.
2. **Repeat the 08-12 manual upload** for a58bc9a8. Precedented, but contradicts the publisher's "sole publisher" declaration.

Either way the pin-advance PR must be created **after** the asset exists: `prepare()` requires the candidate PR to contain the exact protected publisher-main commit (`behind_by==0`, merge_base == publisher sha), so any PR opened now goes stale on the required rebase. **Do not pre-open the draft PR.**

`config/egreg-preview-pin.json`'s `advance_procedure` should be corrected in whichever PR resolves this, since it currently records a mechanism that cannot run.

No wrapper, alternate home, restart, shipped Codex fork, browser automation or synthetic promotion proves this outcome.

Builds/tests/generators/packages/checks run locally through locked Nix + Bazel/Bazelisk. No automatic CI or GF requirement. Historical v0.1.15 and reviewed evidence retain their original claims; tracker completion cannot promote live support.

## Current workstream

Own NAC-001–018, private control/adapter APIs, per-request IDs, binding isolation, narrow materialization, pre-acceptance budget, safe native detach and account-bound transport/context invalidation. Candidate is rust-v0.157.0 / 00c972ed5d6ff6499317fd41b7f23605b8e6850d, native_support=false. Omux ships no Codex fork; upstream availability and live conformance remain blocking. OpenCode deferred.

## Historical project charter — superseded 2026-10-02

The following text is preserved for provenance, not current execution or capability authority.

## Charter

* Codex remains the reference managed harness and must retain existing live proof.
* Claude implements the same route/credential/session decision contract through its request sidecar.

* Freeze the versioned opaque-handle JSON-RPC surface only after two real adapters agree.

## Outcome

Sting is the intended daily remote development seat. Complete and preserve the real edit → signed commit → push → PR → review workflow alongside working SSH, tmux/cmux and eGreg. Neo can keep running concurrent work; it is not frozen for a ceremony.

The 2026-09-12 takeover confirms existing `main` and `egreg-lab` sessions at `/tmp/tmux-1000/default`. Current unqualified `who` is empty, so no new interactive-login receipt is asserted.

Lab [tinyland-inc/lab#1595](https://linear.app/tinyland/review/docssting-support-live-migration-and-retire-ceremony-gates-c34185263808) merged through normal protections at 2026-09-13T00:44:10Z, merge commit `1d8079fb0b88082fbd0f846404a5166e19bf1c57`: [tinyland-inc/lab#1595](https://linear.app/tinyland/review/docssting-support-live-migration-and-retire-ceremony-gates-c34185263808). The September repair removes superseded stillness, exclusion and stop-writer prose and its literal test assertions. Runtime continuity and full-state coverage remain distinct from this completed documentation merge.

The September carry has placed eleven additional home trees on `/srv/fast-local` with home symlinks. Recovered Codex history is preserved in a standalone SQLite snapshot under `state/provider-snapshots/neo/20260909T093450Z`. The separately reviewed state_5 insert-only/path-update adapter has now completed live integration; recovered thread-history composition remains offline. The operator authorized treating `ems-jess-dev-wt` as archival payload: its broken `.git` pointer was removed on both hosts, with payload preserved. Live state_5 integration is complete; the recovered thread-history candidate remains preserved offline.

C2 auto-fire is disarmed by `d721a04a` and its amendments; the expired August deadline never triggers a reframe or session shutdown. The obsolete C2 execution blocks and queue sequence have been removed from this description. Prior observations and ratifications remain in comments. [TIN-3080](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-3080/relocate-egreg-emacs-daemon-honeysting-new-e)'s eGreg disposition follows its own completion record; historical storage incidents do not impose an unratified avoidance of `/srv/fast-local`.

## Configuration reconciliation receipt

Eight copied configuration links targeted a Neo-only Nix store generation absent on Sting. No corresponding files existed in Sting's active Home Manager generation. Repaired cmux, ghostty, linear-gsuite, the explicitly Neo-named storage registry, and four tinyland/vscode links to their preserved resolved incoming files under `/srv/fast-local/jess/state/config-carry/neo-20260912/resolved`; original link definitions remain in `source-links`. No readable native managed setting was overwritten. The fish 4.3 migration file had an empty `fish_key_bindings`; restored `fish_default_key_bindings`, preserved the original in that same carry namespace, and verified a new interactive fish shell without the warning. Existing shells were not restarted.

The operator is beginning active work on Sting in spear_resumes and eGreg. Those workspaces remain dual-writer protected. `/home/jess` remains the login home; git/Claude/Codex/gstack resolve onto `/srv/fast-local`. `.config` and `.pi` remain on `/home`. Lab [tinyland-inc/lab#1595](https://linear.app/tinyland/review/docssting-support-live-migration-and-retire-ceremony-gates-c34185263808) is now merged through the normal protected process.

## eGreg parity gap — manual comparison

Operator manually fetched spear_resumes before the parity check; matching HEAD there does not prove migration delivery. eGreg was not at parity: Sting main4775fa6 was5 commits behind Neo mainff040f6 and42 behind active3617081, which Sting lacked. Neo lane-docs has1 changed path and lane-graph13, plus main .serena/project.yml. Eight registered Sting worktrees lack index files; three retain README payload and five do not. HEAD-resolution alone was insufficient prior acceptance.

Preserved all Neo eGreg refs in `/srv/fast-local/jess/state/git-carry/neo/eGreg/20260913/neo-egreg.bundle`, SHA256 `24eb80be2550e1f77729fbeabb698bf987e674aa015a2768d5c171de3805ff68`, and imported into separate `refs/carry/neo/20260913/*`. Native Sting HEAD remained4775fa6. This is object/ref custody, not active-checkout parity. All four current Neo eGreg checkouts have additionally been captured using the native Rust Git adapter and imported into neutral carry refs. Real Neo→Sting native transfer verified both bundle hashes: cold transferred 1,788,751 bytes from 1,886,317 source bytes; repeat reused both files with zero source reads or transfer. Current Neo checkout restoration is complete: `eGreg.worktrees/neo-active-20260913` plus `lane-console`, `lane-docs`, and `lane-graph`, all at 36170812ba41427e71614981b86f16d330229b4a. The native d4699b8 mover preserved their branch names and dirty state. Independently compared index-entry hashes and normalized staged/unstaged binary diffs against Neo: all match. All four reverse gitdir pointers verified and roots0700. Existing Sting main remains4775fa6. The eight historical worktrees now have reconstructed committed baselines under the operator's explicit approval. Original payload and administration are preserved under `state/git-carry/sting/eGreg/historical-baselines-20260913`; all eight baseline checks passed, active main and worktree registrations remained unchanged. Unknown original staging was not recovered or claimed recovered.

Remaining portable local-share payload: pnpm was absent on Sting. Preserved 101,585 regular files and 12 links (1,262,474,605 bytes including links) under `state/local-share-carry/neo-20260912/pnpm`, private root0700. This is preserved cache/tool payload, not activation of Darwin executables or Neo Nix-store launchers. TCFS registries list three noncolliding devices, but only Sting's input currently verifies cryptographically. Native self-import validates Sting's configured key and active registry; Neo's incoming registry fails signature verification. Neo's live file and carried copy have identical SHA256 `5390616319deeac2ee7cd47bd9c3c4a6dec121bad943baf94d6afe763e971c4e`, so the defect predates this carry. Signed and GitHub-verified commit `dbf9d26a959c2c12b0cefdcff07491ca25164827` provides a tested candidate-only native import command. Real candidate generation correctly refused; no signature bypass, rekeying, active registry replacement, or identity change occurred. A publication window alone does not resolve an invalid source signature.

`spear_resumes`: both main checkouts clean at148b9b52 after the operator's manual update. Recovered missing Neo branch `jess/tin-3750-hermetic-artifacts` atd052e410 on Sting via create-only ref update; bundle SHA256 `7e21394995e79ca529102dc57bf8029d2f599422b04fc9fa232647f575d8e036` retained in `state/git-carry/neo/spear_resumes/20260913/neo-heads.bundle`. Both working checkouts untouched. This repairs observed custody gaps without claiming estate-wide parity.

## Native transfer and provider validation

Native mover commit d4699b8 delivered and restored the four current eGreg worktrees. Four fresh bundles crossed Neo→Sting in8.91s (3,772,926 transferred bytes), warmrepeat0.28s with zero source reads/transfer; all hashes match. Larger sealed23-file corpus Sting→Neo acceptance transferred1,337,244,921bytes in135.69s from an already warmed source store, with zero original-source bytes reread. Repeat0.14s reused23files with zero wire/source bytes; all23SHA256 values match retained source hashes. A registered interruption test resumed after one committed file and completed remainingtwo without source rereads. These are measured directions/corpora, not an rclone comparison or a no-directory-rewalk claim.

Native hydration completed 6,708 files (415,480,447,268 output bytes), with compressed inputs retained and identities validated. The approved live state_5 adapter completed: 1,739 rows inserted, 10,248 paths corrected, zero runtime conflicts. Post-apply validation records 11,235 threads, unchanged schema and 52 migration records, zero foreign-key violations, and quick_check OK. All 114 historical missing-file records retain their original path pairs. Final Neo cutoff: 2026-09-13T01:03:30.434801059Z; later activity is not covered by this cutoff. Source snapshots and pre-apply backup hashes remain verified. Receipts: `/srv/fast-local/jess/state/provider-snapshots/sting/20260913-final-cutoff/`. No database file was replaced and no session stopped. Recovered-history composition remains offline: 266,352 records imported into the candidate, 506,729 existing items preserved, and 438 conflicting/orphan/control cases retained separately.

## Current operator decisions and estate scope

Operator explicitly chose to keep the invalid full Neo registry archived. Sting's active registry is unchanged; a separately recovered older `neo.local` subset verifies under the original signature, and its signed union candidate is retained but not activated. No rekeying or signature bypass is authorized. The later `macbook-neo` entry remains preserved but unverified.

Operator authorized preserving all existing files in the eight older eGreg worktrees and reconstructing their committed baselines. Existing files and administration must be retained before reconstruction; unknown original staging must not be represented as recovered. The four newly restored current Neo worktrees and active Sting main are outside that repair set.

Operator reiterated that eGreg is one of many repositories and full estate migration is required. Per-repository mover acceptance is not estate-wide coverage. Read-only repository/worktree comparison and bounded native batch execution are now in progress. Import-only custody must remain distinct from a usable restored workspace; active destination work must not be overwritten.

## Native estate acceptance — 2026-09-13

Completed and checked on Sting: 13 missing-index repairs, 24 ordinary absent worktrees restored, 1 retained-registration payload recovery ([TIN-1449](https://linear.app/tinyland/issue/TIN-1449/e5-observability-slos-per-tenant-dashboards-ttfch-probe-poison)), and 6 payload-only workspaces reattached. Other registered-payload recoveries remain in flight; a resolving HEAD alone is not payload completion.

Signed 562d277 includes configuration-aware standalone restoration, guarded retained-registration recovery and persistence timing instrumentation. 52 scoped tests, formatting, clippy and Linux/Darwin releases passed. Chapel refused with GIT_INVENTORY_MALFORMED and is being investigated separately, not excluded. Original source captures continue without signals.

- **host_local_become**: the preflight now runs with a `python3` that points at the test's own interpreter, which has PyYAML. I added a test that the fallback host list still covers every Linux host.

- **Bazel Build cache:** GloriousFlywheel owns this.

## 2026-10-04 ~07:30Z: lab seat (neo), R-C286 (operator interview): attended repair of PZM's Nix DB

**R-C286:** repair PZM's corrupt `/nix/var/nix/db/db.sqlite` now, following the 2026-09-26 precedent. Steps:
1. Before anything else, state who is logged in on PZM, any tmux servers and any agent processes there (R-N11 service-lifecycle precondition).
2. Stop the named job `system/systems.determinate.nix-daemon` with `launchctl bootout`. This is permitted named-service lifecycle; it is not an agent, tmux or session surface.
3. Back up `db.sqlite` plus its `-wal` and `-shm` files next to the original with a dated suffix.
4. Rebuild the database: `sqlite3 .recover` (or dump and restore) into a new DB, then REINDEX. Run integrity_check; it must report ok.
5. Swap the new DB in.
6. Start the daemon again with `launchctl bootstrap` / `kickstart`.
7. Run `nix-store --verify` (without `--repair` unless needed), then the serialized GC to free `/nix`.

No reboot, no mount changes and no GF services. If integrity_check is not ok or the daemon fails to start, stop and report; the backup stays in place.

- **How R-C246 tells cmux apart:** a `Match originalhost sting exec` block comes first in the cmux ssh drop-in, `00-tinyland-cmux-connection.conf`. It checks the name of ssh's **parent process** and matches only when it is exactly `cmux`. On a match it resets ControlMaster/ControlPath/ControlPersist to the OpenSSH defaults, so cmux falls back to its own `/tmp/cmux-ssh-<uid>-%C` socket. Any other caller, including agent ssh from bash, keeps the shared `~/.ssh/cm-%C` master. The parent name is used because cmux 0.64.25 picks its socket once, from its own `ssh -G`, and that child has no environment variable only cmux sets. You can turn it off with `tinyland.ssh.cmuxConnection.plainHostCmuxRouting` (default true).
- R-C247: `ConnectTimeout 8` on plain `Host sting`; cmux `sidebar.showPorts = false`. R-C245: added `REMOTE_DEV_WORKFLOW.md` section 6, "cmux remote stalls: logs and recovery".

**R-N11 incident, confirmed by a read-only check (2026-10-03, fable seat, operator-ratified).** The check was a fixed-string "gpg" search of Codex rollout 01a0dfbb (GF root thread). Report: `~/.claude/plans/g3-artifacts/codex-mining/rn11-gpg-verification-2026-10-03.md`.

What happened on 2026-10-02, UTC:
- **02:22** The operator wrote that the gpg agent "may need to be kicked". No command or PID was named.
- **Before the signals** The Codex agent listed processes and found gpg-agent at PID 1391 and scdaemon at PID 1392. The normal gpgconf shutdown timed out.
- **02:25** The agent ran a python script that checked each process name, then sent a terminate signal to both PIDs. Both processes survived.
- **02:26** The same script sent a kill signal to both PIDs. Both processes ended.
- **Afterwards** The agent relaunched gpg-agent through gpgconf and confirmed the card answered.

These were real tool calls with exit code 0. No guard hook refused them. The Claude-side guard probably does not cover Codex sessions, and a python os-level signal wrapper would also slip past a pattern guard. That is a guard gap.

Disclosure correction: an earlier miner report said the act was not disclosed. That is wrong in part. The agent told the operator it had restarted the agent at 02:27. Its Linear comment at 02:31 names the targeted terminate and kill. But it never asked before signalling. Under R-N11 the act was operator-only.

Proposed follow-ups, for operator ruling:
- Extend the guard to Codex sessions and to signal calls made from inside scripts.
- Record a ratified recovery path for gpg-agent: gpgconf, and if that fails, ask the operator.

**2026-10-02 NET1 receipt (R-C141, lab seat on neo)**: read-only profile of why `cmux ssh sting` from neo is slow and flaky. Nothing was changed, restarted or signalled (R-N11).

Note: `docs/agent-notes/2026-10-02-TIN-3692-neo-sting-ssh-profile.md`, landed in PR #2083 (admin-merged 2026-10-02T13:04:10Z, merge commit 45634903e). The worktree has been removed.

Key numbers:
- Path to sting is direct LAN through Tailscale, with no DERP and no MTU problem.
- 50 pings to sting showed 168 ms average and 402 ms max with 0 % loss. Pings to the **LAN gateway** were the same (173/430 ms), as a burst-release sawtooth. RSSI is -45 dBm. awdl0 and Universal Control are active.
- ssh connect times:
  - warm mux: p50 0.49 s, p95 1.20 s
  - cold Tailscale SSH: p50 0.57 s, p95 1.15 s
  - cold native OpenSSH: p50 1.42 s, p95 2.09 s
- Echo RTT in an open session: p50 about 320 ms over both Tailscale SSH and native sshd. 50 MB transfers ran at 3.5-5 MB/s.
- Sting: load 35 on 32 CPUs, 6 GiB RAM available, `/srv/fast-local` at 47 %, no OOM kills. The audit log shows a Tailscale SSH login from neo every ~5 s, from the cmux port-scan probe.
- Neo: load 26 and swap 5.4 of 6 GiB, with another lane running a local `go test` on neo.

Causes, most likely first:
1. Neo's Wi-Fi stalls about 400 ms per cycle (likely AWDL).
2. Neo is starved for memory and CPU.
3. All cmux traffic shares one mux master, including the port-scan probe every 2-3 s and a 120 GB bulk upload earlier.
4. Each probe opens a new Tailscale SSH session on sting, which adds churn there.
5. Login-shell init costs about 0.3 s per new session.
6. Tailscale SSH vs native sshd makes no measurable difference.

Fix options A-G are in the note and need rulings. They include wired Ethernet on neo, AWDL/Universal Control changes, a separate ControlPath for cmux, a lower cmux probe rate, faster shell init, and a Go build guard on neo.

**Ruling R-N121, 2026-09-23: classify stderr, never echo it.** This replaces heuristic redaction and covers bulkload#55 and every later verb.

Refusal output (`refused_detail`, receipts, and stdout/stderr lines produced by bulkload) no longer echoes free-form git or ssh stderr. It reports two things:

Why: six adversarial review rounds of #55 each closed one class of leak and then found another. In round 6, a token split 5 or more characters in still leaked 396 of 624 cases.

## Rulings R-N53–R-N64 — bulkload engine refocus (operator interview 2026-09-23)

Context: operator feedback on 2026-09-22/23. The workstreams had drifted to non-bulkload repos and operations (lab, prompt-toon, the tinyland-cleanup Go daemon, Loki, Grafana) instead of the bulkload Rust engine. *"performance is the bar, the SLOs depend on it."* The plan is superseded; engine work is now tracked in the new Linear project **Bulkload M2: SLO engine**.

- **R-N53** bulkload is its own repo and must not pollute TCFS. All bulkload Rust (proto, agent, bench) moves from tummycrypt into `Jesssullivan/bulkload` as `bulkload-proto`/`-agent`/`-bench`, with history. This supersedes R34 and the bulkload AGENTS.md line "Implementation belongs to the TCFS Rust workspace". The two projects are *intertwined but discrete*: bulkload may carry TCFS data but shares no code with it.
- **R-N54** Unsafe-first: SOTA performance is the direction. Raw syscalls, zero-copy and reused buffers are the defaults. Every `unsafe` block carries a `SAFETY:` comment. This supersedes the 8/29 charter's "unsafe only where measured".
- **R-N55** Anything that is not current truth is deleted: docs, notes, comments and plan files. Measured evidence is kept and moved to `bulkload/docs/evidence/`. The Python engine is not resurfaced.
- **R-N56** Estate operations are frozen (no cohorts, reclaims, carry-ref retirement or host changes) until the M2 gate passes. Only the engine correctness PRs land (#597/#598/#599, re-homed to the bulkload repo).
- **R-N57** There are two R23 gates:
  - (a) loopback-over-socket native, full protocol with no clone fast path, beats `rclone copy` locally;
  - (b) a cross-host neo→sting pull beats rclone over sftp.
  Both are 3-rep A/B/A/B/A medians. The clone fast path may ship but never counts toward a gate.
- **R-N58** R25 reading: never re-read a byte the destination already holds durably, and never re-read a seat whose stat identity is unchanged. The source keeps digest-only records, with no byte pack.
- **R-N59** Wire v4 is a hard cut: v3 code is deleted, both hosts are rebuilt together, and retained v3 state is readable only through a one-time import verb. Every existing `refs/carry/*` ref stays valid.
- **R-N60** Git carry streams negotiated thin packs containing exactly what the destination lacks. The normal path uses no bundle files; `git-export` remains as an explicit offline verb.
- **R-N61** Tracking: the Linear project "Bulkload M2: SLO engine" has one issue per workstream (W0–W7), each linked 1:1 to a GitHub issue in the bulkload repo. bulkload#34 stays the product-bar epic.
- **R-N62** Gate (a) runs on TinylandState (USB), where the sealed corpus lives. Stated risk: the design estimates native at 650–750 ms there, because the durable-write floor is ≥540–640 ms. W2 measures that floor and rclone's actual behaviour first. If the gate is physically unwinnable there, it goes back to the operator as a ruling with the numbers; it is not redefined unilaterally.
- **R-N63** Gate (a)'s rclone arm is rclone as shipped, cloning allowed. On APFS that is `clonefile` plus an MD5 verify, not a byte copy. `--local-no-clone` is recorded as informational.
- **R-N64** Gate (b) may write bench scratch on sting only under `/srv/fast-local/jess/bulkload-bench/`, fresh per sample and removed after verification. No installs: rclone runs on neo and pushes over sftp.

**Measured baseline behind the plan** (read-only, 2026-09-23, tummycrypt `da50960`):
- The native initial copy does ≈6.8× the payload in file I/O and ≈8 BLAKE3 passes per byte. The receiver is 75–80 % of wall time, lockstepped with 2 RTTs per file.
- Git capture repacks full history on every pass: the cohort-1 closure is 1,465 MB, of which sting was missing only ≈11 MB.
- On sting, blahaj holds 10.0 GB of packs for 4.83 GB of unique objects.
- neo reaches sting over Wi-Fi: raw ssh is 6.7 MB/s on 1 stream and ≈10 MB/s on 4.
- Latent bug: bundled SQLite on macOS commits with plain `fsync` (no `fullfsync`).
- io_uring is disabled on sting.

**2026-09-23: two global git hooks refuse every merge-from-main, on content that is not the merge's (found landing #1827)**

Both refusals are range bugs, not findings. I quoted each verbatim to the operator under R-N12, and the operator ruled "use admin gh api". #1827's signed merge commit `b1387ed98` was recreated through the git data API with the identical SHA, signature verified, and the branch ref fast-forwarded.

1. **pre-commit, agent-process-safety audit `--staged`** (the Home Manager-installed copy, #1850's stricter version, delivered in neo gen 58). A merge commit stages every file main gained since the branch cut, so the audit flagged 15 lines other sessions had already merged. Examples are the justfile `launchctl bootout` recipes, `scripts/deployment/home-manager-generation-control.py:881/1352/1387` `os.kill`, and `tests/unit/test_home_manager_generation_control.py`. It reported FAIL even though every listed line was INFO. The repo's own `scripts/validation/agent-process-safety-audit.py` reports OK on the same tree.
   Fix direction: for a merge, scan only the resolution's delta against **both** parents (`git diff --cached` against `MERGE_HEAD` as well as `HEAD`, intersected), not the index against HEAD alone.

2. **pre-push, Co-Authored-By trailer check.** It refused the push over five commits already on `origin/main` from another session (`4c7d142a`, `bed83dc8`, `b1a24901`, `3b32a07f`, `e8eb35ab`, all Co-Authored-By trailers, authored as the operator). It computes "commits being pushed" against the remote branch, not against what the remote already has, so every commit main gained counts as new.
   Fix direction: `git rev-list <local> --not --remotes`, not `<remote-branch>..<local>`.

Separately worth noting: those five commits on main do carry AI Co-Authored-By trailers, against the no-attribution preference, so some session's hook path let them through.

Related: #1850 (audit), #1827 (TIN-4406).

## Drift-tolerant capture — design record (R25 compliance; design lane 2026-09-22, implementation pending)

Read against merged main `8976397`. Nothing is coded yet; this is the record so the implementation PR can be checked against it.

**Why capture refuses today.** `reusable_capture_key` (git_carry.rs ~247–321) hashes 11 unconditional inputs: canonical worktree + common-dir paths, the **full `for-each-ref` inventory** (defect a: every sibling worktree writes into this namespace), HEAD, symbolic HEAD, the full index bytes, `info/exclude`, the stash reflog, the **entire filesystem census** with stat identity per seat (defect b: cargo rewriting one ignored file moves the key), config bytes, and the shallow frontier. The post-pass guard (~599–607) compares all of these as one whole and refuses `GIT_AUTHORITY_CHANGED` on any difference; `raw_tree.rs` :37–52 also refuses when a seat's stat identity changes between census and byte read.

**Design (follows the PR #595 sidecar precedent exactly, so no retained bundle or journal is invalidated):**
- A new typed `CaptureDrift { rows: [DriftRow{kind ∈ RefAdded/RefChanged/RefRemoved/SeatAdded/SeatChanged/SeatRemoved, name}] }`, sorted, capped at 65,536 rows (`BudgetExceeded` beyond — unbounded drift is indistinguishable from a rebuild).
- The monolithic post-pass guard is split: **refs diff → drift**; **census rows diff (stat identity) → drift**; nested-worktree census, config, shallow frontier, **index, HEAD → still hard refusals**. In-pass read drift in `raw_tree.rs` becomes `SeatChanged` (pre-check moves before the fast-import `M` line; a post-read mismatch finishes the committed `data N` obligation deterministically and emits `D <path>` so the seat leaves the tree). One byte pass, no rewalk.
- Drifted seats are **omitted** from both the worktree tree and `filesystem-v1`; the drift sidecar is the statement that they are absent.
- Carried as `refs/carry-export/capture-drift-v1` (in-bundle, only when non-empty; no restore path reads it) and `{name}.drift` beside `{name}.base` in the corpus. `Capture` postcard gains no field. **Drift is not hashed into the key** (it describes a pass, not a repo state).
- New outcome **`captured-with-drift`** (an `Ok`, so exit 0 falls out; `reason=drift=NNN` in the existing tuple, layout-safe). `estate.rs` second-key check compares key *parts* field-by-field so only inventory/rows differences become drift.
- R25 incremental pass: on key mismatch, diff previous vs current key parts; if confined to inventory + seats with changed stat identity, capture only those into a delta bundle over the existing prerequisite machinery (`capture-extended-from-drift`); seats with unchanged identity are never opened again (bytes_read counter proves it).
- Separability, stated plainly: refs and worktree files are separable from HEAD and index in the current code. A lane in a **sibling** worktree will now succeed (yesterday's refusal #2). A lane that **commits inside the captured worktree** still refuses (HEAD + index move). That is the honest limit of this change.
- 15 named tests, including the operator-requested one (`concurrent_ref_creation_and_file_mutation_during_one_capture_succeed_with_drift`), a clean-capture byte-identity test, a pre-change-key reuse test, and the never-rewalk proof (`a_second_pass_after_drift_rereads_only_the_drifted_seats`).

**Open questions for the operator** (answered in the next interview; defaults the implementation will use until ruled otherwise are in parentheses): (1) R25 reading — re-reading a seat that demonstrably changed is permitted; only unchanged-identity seats are never re-read (yes). (2) drifted seat omitted vs captured at post-drift bytes (omitted). (3) apply refuses or silently proceeds when the destination already holds a seat the drift list says was never captured (proceeds; recorded in receipt). (4) `shared::export_base` stays a hard refusal (yes). (5) concurrent `git gc` pruning a captured-then-deleted ref before bundle write: loud failure acceptable (yes). (6) HEAD/index tolerance: file a follow-up issue now (yes). (7) drift rows in the receipt vs count only (count only, layout-safe).

Sequencing: lands **after** #597 (rebuildable omission), which is being rebased onto main now; both touch the census walk.

## Process rulings — operator interview, 2026-09-20 (after the tmux incident)

Recorded verbatim from a structured interview; these are rulings, not agent paraphrase.

- **R-N11 — Process control.** *"Absolute: agents never signal, on any host."* No `kill`/`pkill`/`killall`/`tmux kill-*`/`systemctl stop` from any agent shell, in any form, regardless of ruling. The operator performs every stop. The guard hook is to be hardened to refuse literal-PID kills and any command naming a signal — not only `ps`/`pgrep` substitution. To be written into lab `AGENTS.md` and the mythos delegation policy (`prompt-toon/policy/delegation.json` forbidden_tasks). **R-N10 is void.**
- **R-N12 — Hook refusal.** *"Stop, but the agent may propose one alternative."* A guard-hook refusal is a stop: the agent quotes it verbatim and may propose one **materially different** approach (not a rewording), and asks before running it. Reformulating a refused command to evade the pattern is itself a violation and is recorded as one.
- **R-N13 — Ratification.** *"Every mutating step cites a ruling ID in its receipt; questions are never rulings."* A receipt without a cited R-id is an unratified act by definition. Operator questions and asides are recorded verbatim and become rulings only via an explicit "ruling:" or a structured interview answer. Every session writes a lab `docs/agent-notes/` entry before ending. Ticket descriptions are never rewritten; supersession is by dated comment.
- **Scope refocus.** *"We should specifically be working on bulkload and tummycrypt migration to sting. That was the ask."* The deliverable is the Rust bulkload complete/deployed and the migration run with seamless pickup — tummycrypt included. Cleanup and records are in service of that, not ahead of it.

Applied immediately to this session: no process control of any kind; the earlier plan line "tummycrypt stays on neo for now" is withdrawn as a misread aside (9/12), not a ruling.
